The time and location of each meeting/hearing is identified.
Published hearing transcripts contain all witness testimony, the question-and-answer portion of the hearing, and any other material requested of the witness by the committee.
It may take several months, or even years, for a hearing to be published.
Unlike most other congressional documents, hearings are not available from the Senate or House Document Rooms.
You may be able to locate a hearing from the Government Publishing Office's govinfo website, from a committee website, or from a federal depository library.
For more tips, read the guide How to find committee hearings.
